Both social and instrumental form of interactions elicit genuine emotional responses in users. AI systems that support human decision-making contribute to reducing uncertainty and generating positive experiences. Such interactions foster the development of functional regulatory dependence on AI tools and systems. This article integrates theoretical perspectives and empirical findings on human-AI interaction by proposing a feedback loop model. The model highlights intolerance of uncertainty and inertial thinking as key mechanisms determining reliance on AI in decision-making processes and the development of dependence on these systems. The proposed framework provides a theoretical basis for future research on the psychological consequences of AI use.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7008244\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6147327\", \"title\": [\"Trust Amplification Exploits in Human to AI Security Teams Abusing Overconfidence in Automated Recommendations\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Human-AI collaboration has become a central component of modern cybersecurity operations. Security analysts increasingly rely on automated systems for threat detection, risk assessment, and incident response.
